{"edits": [{"finding_ids": ["test_codes-failure"], "search": "    "field required": "MISSING",
    "value is not a valid integer": "NOT_AN_INTEGER",
    "ensure this value has at least": "TOO_SHORT",", "replace": "    "Field required": "MISSING",
    "Input should be a valid integer": "NOT_AN_INTEGER",
    "String should have at least": "TOO_SHORT",", "explanation": "The test failed because the MESSAGE_CODES keys are Pydantic v1 error message text. Pydantic v2 changed the default messages: a missing field is now "Field required" (capitalized), an int parse failure is "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer", and a min_length failure is "String should have at least N characters". Since lookup uses err["msg"].startswith(m), the v1 keys never matched and every error fell through to "INVALID". The keys are updated to the v2 message prefixes; the public codes (MISSING, NOT_AN_INTEGER, TOO_SHORT) are unchanged. The @field_validator migration from the previous attempt is kept as-is."}], "notes": "The failing test is caused by v1 error-message strings in MESSAGE_CODES, not by the validator. Pydantic v2 emits different default messages (for example \"Field required\" instead of \"field required\", and \"Input should be a valid integer...\" instead of \"value is not a valid integer\"), so no key matched and every error became INVALID. I updated only the three mapping keys to the v2 message prefixes and kept the public code values. The original @validator finding (app/api_errors.py:10:validator) was already fixed by the previous attempt, which uses @field_validator with @classmethod, so I did not touch it. No new imports are needed. I did not run the test suite, so the expected output is inferred from the v2 message format."}
